question.text: An AMC wishes to undertake a business activity unrelated to fund management. Under SEBI regulations, this is:

answer.text: Permitted only with prior approval from SEBI
Permitted freely as long as it does not impair fund management
Permitted with approval from the Board of Trustees only

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, an AMC is required to confine itself to the activity of asset management for mutual funds and related advisory services. Undertaking any unrelated business activity is not permitted without prior approval from SEBI. The regulator gates such expansion to preserve the AMC's fiduciary focus on unitholders and to ensure no conflict of interest, capital, or operational risk leaks into the mutual fund vehicle. The Trap: "Permitted freely as long as it does not impair fund management" ignores the requirement for regulatory clearance. "Absolutely prohibited under all circumstances" is too rigid — SEBI does allow diversification on a case-by-case basis. "Approval from the Board of Trustees only" is incorrect because trustee approval alone does not authorise a business line change of this nature; SEBI's prior approval is required. Note: The cited pages of the NISM Series V-A Mutual Fund Distributors workbook (p.65-p.66, p.73) do not explicitly state that AMC business activities unrelated to fund management require prior SEBI approval. The framing above reflects general SEBI Mutual Fund Regulations and industry practice for AMC scope-of-activity restrictions.
